name: Example: Finding Unit Tangent Vectors Using the Rules of Differentiation For Vector Functions
problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $\mathbf r(t)=e^{2t}\mathbf p(t)$ at the point where $t=0,$ if $\mathbf p(0)=\mathbf i-\,\mathbf j-\mathbf k$ and $\mathbf p'(0)=\mathbf i - \mathbf j+ 2\mathbf k.$
worked_solution:
For a curve $\mathbf r(t)=x(t)\mathbf i+y(t)\mathbf j+z(t)\mathbf k,$ the unit tangent vector $\mathbf T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
\mathbf T(t)=\dfrac{\mathbf r'(t)}{\left\| \mathbf r'(t) \right\|}.
$$

First, we find $\mathbf r'(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{2t}p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{2t})p(t)+{e}^{2t}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & =2{e}^{2t}p(t)+{e}^{2t}{p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(0) & =2{e}^{2(0)}p(0)+{e}^{2(0)}{p}^{′}(0) \\  & =2(i-\,j-k)+1(i-j+2k) \\  & =3\,i-3\,j\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we calculate the magnitude of $\mathbf r'(0)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(0)‖ & =\sqrt{(3)^{2}+(-3)^{2}+(0)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2\cdot {3}^{2}} \\  & =3\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize $\mathbf r'(0)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(0)}{‖{r}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}}(3\,i-3\,j) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(i-j) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(i-j)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=0$ is $\mathbf T(0) = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(\mathbf i -  \mathbf j).$
